name: owen-g-glenn-building
estimated: some heights, with a photograph as a reference; the crown's width; the top of the strip between the west wing and the curved wing, which the LiDAR does not see; and the faces no photograph shows, the curved wing's drawn after the ones it shows and the rest plainly
refs_note: the folder of refs/ that holds the reference views (views.json, masks/), which refine, compare, metrics, sky_mask and the viewer's ?sv= read: refs/photos (gitignored), whose views tools/photo_camera.py writes. Its one photograph is taken from the north edge of the raised plaza north-east of the curved wing, about 1.2 m above the plaza, looking south across a raised lawn at the wing's inner face and the sloping canopy before it, up 10 degrees through a lens of about 60 degrees across; its camera is fitted to the canopy's low edge, three corners of the lawn, the crown of louvres on the wing's east arm and five upright edges, with the principal point at the centre. A second, smaller picture laid over the photograph's bottom right corner is left out of its view (photo_camera's exclude).

building.title: Sir Owen G Glenn Building (260), University of Auckland
building.note: outline: building 260's outer ring from the main project's campus.json, in the map's frame; it chooses the crop box and the building's own points (frame.near_outline, measure and topview). The site replaces block 260 by its id.

origin.note: the campus origin, as in campus.json; the landmark's local metres = NZTM (EPSG:2193) minus the NZTM of this point, with grid north

door.note: the front under the sloping canopy in the curve's inner corner, as the photograph shows it: a glazed front the height of the ground storey, a banner in it and a dark wall with lettering beside it, on the plaza; its doors are not made out (the campus map records no lobby or entrance in 260, only a reception on level 0, below the plaza, and OpenStreetMap no entrance near it). The door is set on the plaza 1.5 m out from the middle of the canopy's low edge, under its edge (u 2.98, w 4.31 in the building's frame). The LiDAR's ground within 1 m: 17 returns, p10/p50/p90 29.595/29.621/29.673 m

frame.method: LiDAR building points (class 6) more than min_above m above the ground and within near_outline m of building.outline
frame.thresholds_note: min_above, tower_above and spine_below were 3, 3 and 40 m above the provisional ground (24.46 m); lowered by 5.16 m with the ground set at the door, so that they pick the same points and the measured frame stays the expected one

ground_note: the LiDAR's ground at the door (step 7, 2026-11-09); the provisional ground was 24.46 m, the median LiDAR ground in the crop box, from which the heights in parts/common.js are measured (its H moves them on to this ground)

light.note: estimated: the photograph is taken in the late morning of 12 December 2018 (its own record), the viewer's sun where the sun then stood, 61.7 deg round and 65.8 deg up; the exposure from the building's luma on the door's ground (the parts more than 4 m above it): p10/p50/p90 79/160/241 at 1.5 against the photograph's 104/164/235, with round 1's faces
